title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for hard floor care
audience: Owners of hard floor care businesses, including solo operators, who quote per square metre for timber and other hard floors in homes and small commercial spaces.
learningOutcomes: Write an offer with a clear promised outcome, time frame and conditions
Identify the friction and risk the customer carries and reduce them
Price the offer on value and cost, not only time

instruction.heading: A bad offer versus a good offer for a hard floor
instruction.body: 'Floor polish, $25 a square metre' is a price, not an offer. 'Polish of the measured floor area in the finish you choose, with a condition check and photos before work, a stated drying time, and a return visit for any listed defect' is an offer. The client buys a floor that matches the agreed finish, and a scope they can check.

instruction.heading: The five parts of a hard floor offer
instruction.body: Set the outcome (the agreed finish on the measured area), the time frame (your timed work plus the cure or dry time you set), what the client must do (move furniture, give access, report earlier finishes and damage), the certainty you give (condition check, photos, a measurement sheet) and the risk you carry (a return visit for listed defects). A written quote becomes binding once accepted (business.gov.au, 1 August 2025). WA guidance says a quote should set out the job, possible extra costs, materials, labour and time to finish (WA only).

instruction.heading: Assess condition before you quote
instruction.body: Oneflare's guide says a poor-condition surcharge adds about $10 to $20 per square metre or more (undated, 2025 prices). That is a vendor figure for polishing and sanding. Show any condition surcharge as its own line, and only after you have inspected the floor. Its finish prices also differ widely: solvent polyurethane $12 to $20 per square metre, water-based polyurethane $8 to $17, oil-based varnish $8 to $12 and wax $6 to $10 (same source). Name the finish on the quote.

instruction.heading: Measure, show one total, and say what is not included
instruction.body: Measure length times width, including alcoves, as the Oneflare guide describes, and write the method on the quote. Show one total including GST and say whether GST is included (business.gov.au, 18 January 2024; WA guidance for WA). The Oneflare figures are for polishing and sanding, not routine cleaning, and the research found no cleaning-only price. Say on the quote what is included.

instruction.heading: Deposit and guarantee
instruction.body: If you take a deposit, WA guidance says it should generally be no more than 10 per cent (WA only; 4 September 2026). Offer a fix-first return visit for listed defects. Under the consumer guarantees a business must be given a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault free of charge (Consumer Victoria's guidance, 13 October 2023; a Victorian page, so check your state's consumer agency). That page sets no fix window. A 'no refunds' line does not override service rights (business.gov.au, 27 May 2025).

procedure: Write the outcome in one sentence for the agreed area and finish.
Measure the area as length times width, including alcoves, and record the method.
Inspect the floor, and record its condition, previous finishes and any defects before you quote.
Set each quote line: area, finish, condition work and any separate defect repair.
Price from timed work and your costs, then compare with the vendor range and state which one you used.
Write the exclusions, the drying time, the client's inputs and the validity date, and agree extra work in writing before doing it.

workedExamples.situation: [ILLUSTRATIVE] A cleaner is asked to polish a 50 square metre timber floor in a Victorian house. The floor is in good condition. The client has seen prices of $1,250 to $3,000 for a floor of this size.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What range can the cleaner show, and what must be checked before the quote is sent?
workedExamples.reasoning: The Oneflare page gives a whole-job range of $1,250 to $3,000 for 50 square metres (undated, 2025 prices). It also gives a Victorian labour cost of $20 to $30 per square metre, which is $1,000 to $1,500 for 50 square metres (CALC). The two ranges do not reconcile, and the source does not explain the gap, so the cleaner does not quote either one as a price. The cleaner prices from timed work, names the finish, shows the area measurement and the drying time, and adds a condition surcharge as its own line only if the inspection shows one. Both ranges are for polishing and sanding, so the cleaner does not use them for a cleaning-only job, which the research did not price.

commonErrors.error: Using the polishing range as the price for a cleaning-only job.
commonErrors.prevention: Price cleaning from your own timed work. The research found no cleaning-only price.

commonErrors.error: Quoting per square metre with no measured area.
commonErrors.prevention: Measure length times width, including alcoves, and write the method on the quote.
Inspect before you quote and show any condition work as its own line.
Name the finish on the quote, because the vendor's finish prices differ widely.

commonErrors.error: Treating a directory total as a fixed price.
commonErrors.prevention: Reconcile the figures and price from your own inputs.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Business guidance only. This lesson does not grant any licence. Licence rules for hard floor work were not researched, so check the rules for your state or territory before you offer the work.
Price display: show the total including GST (business.gov.au, 18 January 2024). WA guidance on quotes and deposits applies in Western Australia only.

Consumer guarantees for services cannot be removed by contract (business.gov.au, 27 May 2025). The Victorian consumer page cited for the fix-first point is Victorian guidance, so check your state's consumer agency.

qualityStandard: Offer and pricing decisions are written down and checked against cost and time.
documentationEvidence: Written offer or plan, evidence collected, and the decision made.
summary: Quote hard floor work for a measured area, a named finish and a checked condition.
The vendor totals and per-square-metre ranges are for polishing and sanding, and they do not reconcile. Price from your own timed work.
Gaps: cleaning-only prices, minimum charges, sanding dust and safety rules, and strata and agent channels were not sourced.

knowledgeChecks.question: What makes a hard floor quote clear to a client?
options: A per-square-metre price with no area, finish or condition stated
The measured area, the named finish, the condition check and the exclusions
A promise that the floor will look new

knowledgeChecks.question: A vendor gives a $1,250 to $3,000 range for a 50 square metre polish, and the same source gives a Victorian labour range that works out lower. What should you do?
options: Quote the midpoint of the two
Point out that the ranges do not reconcile and price from your own timed work
Quote the lower figure without checking the scope

knowledgeChecks.question: Before a hard floor job starts, what should you record about the floor?
options: Its condition, previous finishes and any defects

sourceReferences: Oneflare (Airtasker co-brand), 'Floor polishing cost', https://www.oneflare.com.au/costs/floor-polishing, undated ('2025 prices'). Vendor marketplace; covers polishing and sanding, not routine cleaning. Supports: per square metre ranges, state labour rates, finish prices, a poor-condition surcharge and whole-job totals.

WA Consumer Protection, 'Ask us: Estimates and quotes', https://consumerprotection.wa.gov.au/publications/ask-us-estimates-and-quotes, last updated 18 November 2024. Western Australia only. Supports: a quote is a fixed price and an estimate can move; extra work needs the customer's permission; a written quote should state the job, possible extra costs, materials, labour and time to finish.

WA Consumer Protection, 'Estimates, quotes and deposits', https://www.consumerprotection.wa.gov.au/estimates-quotes-and-deposits, last updated 4 September 2026. Western Australia only. Supports: show the total including GST and say whether GST is included; a deposit should generally be no more than 10 per cent; extra work needs written approval.

business.gov.au, 'Prepare quotes', https://business.gov.au/people/contractors/prepare-quotes, last updated 1 August 2025. Supports: a written quote becomes binding once accepted; a quote should recover cost plus a margin.
business.gov.au, 'Display prices', https://business.gov.au/legal/fair-trading/display-prices, page metadata 18 January 2024. Supports: displayed prices should show the total price, including GST.

Consumer Victoria, 'Services not done with due care and skill', https://www.consumer.vic.gov.au/products-and-services/problem-with-a-service/services-not-done-with-due-care-and-skill, last updated 13 October 2023. Victoria. Supports: a business should be given a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault free of charge; the page sets no fix-window length.

Comcare, 'Bathroom cleaning products', https://www.comcare.gov.au/office-safety-tool/spaces/bathrooms/bathroom-cleaning-products, no date shown. Supports: obtain the safety data sheet (SDS) for each product, keep original labels, use the PPE the SDS specifies, and follow label directions. The page covers bathroom products only.

business.gov.au, 'Warranties and refunds', https://www.business.gov.au/Products-and-services/Fair-trading/Warranties-and-refunds, last updated 27 May 2025. Supports: an optional warranty sits on top of the consumer guarantees; a 'no refunds' line does not override a customer's rights for services.

ACCC, 'Setting prices: what's allowed', https://www.accc.gov.au/business/pricing/setting-prices-whats-allowed, page last modified 15 July 2026. Supports: misleading statements about prices are prohibited.

Notes: the $1,000 to $1,500 range is CALC on the Oneflare Victorian labour rate. The Oneflare figures are undated 2025 vendor prices for polishing and sanding. The Comcare page covers bathroom products only.
